A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distractor-generation study. Their complete main text, four figures, Tables 1–30 and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original ranker and generator experiments, human evaluations and appendix ablations, including accuracy results in Table 3 and student-study outcomes in Table 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental and human-study outcomes, including Tables 3–16 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: The ranker, student-choice dataset construction and distractor generator retain the same procedures, reasoning outputs, distractor-type prediction and SFT/DPO training. The appendix prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same base Python, DB and MLDL coverage, generated CS questions and 88 English-exam questions. v3 identifies the existing English source as CSAT; this documents provenance without establishing different coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding experiments, including Scarlatos et al. for ranking, Feng et al. and Hang et al. for generation, and the respective GPT, Mistral and human comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported splits, training counts, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 model, SFT/DPO budgets, evaluation Settings A/B, metrics and human-study designs remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: Both retain the reasoning and dataset ablations, sliding-window pairing comparison, positional-bias analysis, validity and similarity checks, error cases and generalizability experiments. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report ranker results averaged over five generations, plausibility counts averaged over two evaluations and variance in Table 14. Repetition and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched entries in Tables 3–16 and plotted findings in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. For example, both report average DPO rank accuracy of 0.675 in Table 3 and DPO discrimination index of 0.212 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The model mappings in Equations 1–2 and the discrimination-index formula are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about reasoning-based ranking, student-choice training, distractor plausibility, discrimination and ranking performance comparable to human experts.

C2.justification: Interpretations of subject differences and plausibility–validity tradeoffs are retained. The limitations concerning computation, invalid distractors, difficulty adaptation and population-specific misconceptions also remain unchanged, including Appendix E.

D1.justification: Page 1 and Section 3.1 replace a future-release promise with a stated code/data location. v3 adds CSAT selection-rate provenance and identifies Elice as the proprietary-data provider. It omits the earlier 52-question release count and explicit fine-tuned-model release promise; implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior research are unchanged. Adding 'in the education domain' in Section 2.2 clarifies the existing scope; the Baek reference's publisher correction is bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Localized edits update affiliations and author footnotes, refine wording, add dataset explanations and an Acknowledgments section, and correct a publisher name. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Page reflow relocates existing displays, including Table 5 between columns on page 8 and Table 14 from page 15 to page 16. Figure content, table structures and captions are retained; no display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves reproducibility documentation and transparency through code/data access information and clearer dataset provenance. Methods, results and conclusions are unchanged. The release description loses the earlier subset-size specification and fine-tuned-model promise, limiting the gain.
